svg.text: Capacity Estimation Cheat-Sheet: baseline + all 29 questions
Memorize the baseline, then change only the knob that differs. Last column = what to say aloud.
10 KB/req: avg 2 Gbps · peak 120K → 1.2 GB/s ≈ 10 Gbps
1 MB img · 5 MB video · 10M × 1 MB = 10 TB/day → 3.65 PB/yr

avg QPS ≈ 1.2K × actions/day (peak ×5) · every 1% of writes at 2 KB ≈ 40 GB/day (≈ 14.6 TB/yr) · each 1 KB per request at 120K QPS ≈ 1 Gbps · 1B/day ≈ 12K/s, 1B/month ≈ 400/s · DAU ÷ 10 → everything ÷ 10
What to say in the interview
Nothing: use the baseline as is
24K avg / 120K peak · 108K reads / 12K writes · 400 GB/day · media
With 100M DAU and 20 actions a day that's 2B requests a day: about 24K QPS average, 120K at peak, 90:10 reads to writes. 200M writes a day at 2 KB is 400 GB a day,
146 TB a year, 438 TB with 3× replication. Photos: 10M a day at 1 MB is 10 TB a day.
119K reads / 1.2K writes at peak · 1% writes = 20M tweets = 40
Same 100M DAU, 2B requests a day, 24K average and 120K peak, but 99:1 reads to writes: about 119K read and 1.2K write QPS at peak. 20M tweets a day at 2 KB is 40
GB a day, about 15 TB a year. Images: 10M a day at 1 MB, 10 TB a day.
Browsing dominates, so 95:5 reads to writes. Average is 24K QPS but sale days spike 10×, so I size for 240K. Writes are 5%: 100M a day at 2 KB, 200 GB a day. Actual
orders are about 5M a day, roughly 60 a second, with strong consistency on inventory.
Searches dominate: 10 actions a day gives 1B requests a day, about 12K QPS average and 60K at peak, 99:1 reads to writes. That is 10M writes a day at 2 KB, 20 GB a day.
Bookings are a tiny share but need strong consistency, so correctness matters more than QPS.
Read-heavy with 10 actions a day: 1B requests a day, 12K QPS average, 60K at peak, 99:1 reads to writes. Reviews and ratings are about 10M writes a day at 2 KB, 20 GB
a day. Geo search and caching hot businesses carry the load.
5 actions a day gives 500M requests a day: about 6K QPS average and 30K at peak, with 80:20 reads to writes. 100M writes a day at 2 KB is 200 GB a day. Reminders spike
on the hour, so I queue and fan out rather than poll.
24K avg → ≈ 1.2M QPS peak · 10% writes = 120K/s on few seats
Average is the baseline 24K QPS, but a ticket sale spikes about 50×, so I size for 1.2M QPS at peak. If 10% are booking attempts that's 120K a second fighting for a limited
set of seats, so the problem is contention and double-booking, not storage.
12K bids/s peak · one hot auction ≈ 1K bids/s at close · 400 GB/day
Baseline traffic, 24K average and 120K peak, with bids as the 10% writes: about 12K bids a second at peak and 400 GB a day. One hot auction can take about 1K bids a
second in its last seconds, so I serialize bids per item to keep one correct highest bid.
Smaller scale: 10M DAU, 20 actions a day, 200M requests a day, about 2.4K QPS average and 12K at peak. 10% submissions is 1.2K a second at peak; at about 2 seconds
per run that is roughly 2.4K concurrent sandboxes. Storage is 40 GB a day.
60K reads / 60K writes at peak · 1B edits/day × 100 B = 100 GB/day
Editing is write-heavy, 50:50. Baseline 24K average and 120K peak means 60K reads and 60K edits a second at peak. Each edit is small, about 100 B, so 1B edits a day is
100 GB a day. The hard part is conflict resolution, OT or CRDT, not volume.
20 KB per tile, almost all reads
120K × 20 KB = 2.4 GB/s ≈ 20 Gbps · mostly served by a CDN
Almost all traffic is tile reads. At 120K peak QPS and about 20 KB per tile that's 2.4 GB a second, roughly 20 Gbps, served mostly from a CDN. Writes are tiny, mainly traffic
and map updates, so the work is caching and routing.
Baseline 100M DAU, 2B requests a day, 24K average and 120K peak, but 99:1 reads to writes: about 119K reads and 1.2K writes a second at peak. 20M new URLs a day at
2 KB is 40 GB a day, about 15 TB a year. With an 80% cache hit the database sees about 24K reads a second.
100M DAU, 10 searches a day, 5 keystrokes each: 50 requests per user, 5B a day, about 58K QPS average and 290K at peak. Responses are about 1 KB, so roughly 2.4
Gbps at peak. Traffic is read-only; the index is tens of GB, so it fits in memory and I cache hot prefixes.
Sits in front of baseline traffic
120K checks/s ≈ 2 Redis shards · state 100M × 100 B = 10 GB
Every request is checked, so 120K checks a second at peak: about two Redis shards at roughly 100K operations each. State is one counter per user, 100M × 100 B, about
10 GB. The limiter must add under 5 ms, so counters stay in memory and approximate counts are fine.
86K cache / 22K DB · hot 20% of 400 GB = 80 GB ≈ 2 nodes (4 with
With 108K peak reads and an 80% hit ratio the cache serves about 86K a second and 22K reach the database. The hot working set is 20% of a day's 400 GB, 80 GB, which
is two 64 GB nodes, four with replicas. Sub-millisecond reads, consistent hashing for scale.
438 TB ÷ 10 TB/node ≈ 44 nodes · 120K ÷ 10K per node ≈ 12 nodes
A year of data is 146 TB, 438 TB with 3× replication. At 10 TB per node that's about 44 nodes. QPS needs only about 12 nodes, at 120K peak and 10K per node, so storage
drives the node count. I partition by key hash and replicate three ways.
If 1% of the 2B daily actions are payments, that's 20M a day: about 230 a second on average, 1.2K at peak. Each payment writes 2 ledger entries at 2 KB, 80 GB a day,
about 29 TB a year. Volume is modest; correctness, idempotency and an auditable ledger are the challenge.
Orders are the 10% writes: about 12K orders a second at peak, 200M a day at 2 KB, 400 GB a day. Matching is done in memory, one thread per symbol, so the target is
latency of milliseconds or less and strict ordering, not raw volume.
Each action is a 100 B message
Each action is a message: 2B a day, 24K a second on average and 120K at peak. At 100 B each, 200 GB a day, about 73 TB a year. Concurrent users are about 10% of DAU,
10M connections; at 50K per server that's roughly 200 chat servers.
Location updates dominate: 1M active drivers sending a point every 4 seconds is 250K updates a second, about 25 MB a second at 100 B each, roughly twice the baseline
peak. Rides are 1% of 2B, 20M a day, only about 230 a second. I partition by geo cell.
Writes peak at about 12K comments a second. With 1M viewers on one stream, sending every comment to everyone would be 12B deliveries a second, so I batch and
sample. Capping at 10 a second per viewer at 100 B is 1M × 10 × 100 B, 1 GB a second, about 8 Gbps.
About 10% of 100M DAU stream at once: 10M streams at 5 Mbps is 50 Tbps, far beyond an origin, so everything is served from a CDN. Storage: 10K titles at about 50 GB
across encodings is 500 TB. Bandwidth, not QPS, is the bottleneck.
10M × 1.5 Mbps ≈ 15 Tbps upload · egress is several times that
Assume 10% of DAU are in meetings, 10M participants. At about 1.5 Mbps upload each that's 15 Tbps ingress, and egress is several times that because each person
receives several streams. So I use SFU media servers, regional routing and adaptive bitrate.
200M × 1 GB = 200 PB · erasure coding 1.5× ≈ 300 PB (vs 600 PB at
Storage is the story: 200M users at 1 GB each is 200 PB. With 3× replication that's 600 PB, but erasure coding at about 1.5× brings it to roughly 300 PB. Chunking and
deduplication cut it further; sync traffic is small, mostly metadata and deltas.
1B pages a month is about 400 pages a second. At 100 KB each that's 40 MB a second, about 0.3 Gbps, and 100 TB a month raw. It is network-bound, so I use async
fetchers sharded by host for politeness, and compress to cut storage.
12K/s avg, 60K peak · midnight 18% in 60 s = 3M/s (259×) · 1 TB
1B jobs a day is about 12K a second on average, 60K at a 5× peak. But if 18% fire at midnight within 60 seconds, that's 180M over 60 s, 3M a second, about 259× the
average, so I size for the spike. 1B pending jobs at 1 KB is about 1 TB.
12K/s avg, 60K peak · 200 B raw = 200 GB/day ≈ 73 TB/yr
1B clicks a day is about 12K a second, 60K at peak. Raw events at 200 B are 200 GB a day, about 73 TB a year. Aggregates are tiny by comparison, so I stream-process,
deduplicate for exactly-once counts, and keep raw events cold.
12K/s (60K peak) · exact 100M items × 16 B ≈ 1.6 GB · sketch: MBs
1B views a day is about 12K events a second, 60K at peak. Exact counters for 100M items at 16 B each are about 1.6 GB, which fits in memory; a count-min sketch plus a
heap needs only megabytes if approximate results are acceptable.
≈ 12 articles/s × 100 KB = 100 GB/day · readers use the baseline
Ingest is small: 1M articles a day is about 12 a second, at 100 KB that's 100 GB a day. The read side is a normal feed, so I reuse the baseline: 24K QPS average, 120K peak.
Freshness and deduplication quality matter more than volume.
Assumptions (drivers, sandbox time, bitrates) are mine: say each one aloud before using it.
